paper.title: Broadband highly-efficient dielectric metadevices for polarization control
paper.authors: Kruk, Hopkins, Kravchenko, Miroshnichenko, Neshev, Kivshar

meta.target_figure: Fig. 3(a) transmission along both pillar axes

Si.name: Si (Silicon) - Palik
Si.cite: text: polycrystalline silicon on quartz; no poly-Si entry in the database

assumptions: a and b are taken as FULL diameters of the elliptical cross-section: with D = 750 nm a semi-axis interpretation would give b = 900 nm > period, which is impossible.
Silicon modelled with the crystalline Palik entry; the paper uses polycrystalline Si and states no optical constants. Expect a small index offset.
Fig. 2 quotes a=285, b=450, c=860 nm while the Fig. 3 text quotes a=280, b=430, c=850 nm for the half-wave plate. The Fig. 3 values are used because that is the target figure.
Substrate truncated to 1 um; a 1 um quartz layer is opaque over the C+L band only in the sense that it is transparent — it is the propagation medium, so the thickness is not critical.
Light is incident from the substrate side and collected in air, matching the standard transmission measurement for an on-glass metasurface.

Fig. 3(a) shows transmission for polarizations along both pillar axes; the sweep over pol = 0 deg and 90 deg supplies the two curves. Which axis maps to 0 deg is unstated, so the two spectra are labelled by angle only.

missing.question: Which refractive index data was used for the LPCVD polycrystalline silicon? Crystalline Palik differs from poly-Si mainly by grain-boundary absorption.
Is the ellipse major axis aligned with x or y? The paper states polarization is 'parallel to the short axis' in Fig. 2 without defining the axis orientation.
Was the quartz substrate included in the FDTD domain, or replaced by an index-matched port?
